newsitem.title: UK: AWB sees up to 20 mln ts 97/98 wheat.
newsitem.headline: AWB sees up to 20 mln ts 97/98 wheat.

text.p: Australian Wheat Board (AWB) chairman Trevor Flugge says Australia could produce a wheat crop of up to 20 million tonnes in 1997/98 but adds that the weather might put "considerable downside" on this forecast.

The AWB in Sydney issued a summary of remarks by Flugge prepared for delivery at a London meeting of the International Grains Council (IGC) in which he also expects world wheat demand to outstrip supply in 1997/98, leading to a likely drawdown on stocks.
The summary quoted him as saying that, with growers intending to plant 11 million hectares of wheat, Australia was capable of producing a crop of up to 20 million tonnes.

"However, at this early stage of crop development it must be recognised that there can be considerable downside in this forecast given the normal variability of climatic conditions in Australia and the prediction of a likely El Nino event over the next 12 months," he said.
Flugge was quoted as saying that he expects export availability from the five major wheat exporters to be down from 1996/97 levels.
"Lower production, combined with strong demand in Asia and drought conditions in parts of Africa are likely to ensure that import demand will remain relatively strong," Flugge says.
He adds that the medium-term outlook for wheat is positive but more volatile.

"As we rely more and more on actual production of each season, rather than the level of stocks to determine market prices, I believe we will witness an increase in the level of volatility in the international market," he is quoted as saying.
